first_impression.reaction: I typed 'greece wedding packages' on the train. The first line is a bit of a lead-in, but the second sentence tells me what a package usually covers and the third tells me where they differ. That's my answer in under 60 words. The takeaways repeat it in four bullets, so I'd read those, tap into 'What packages often leave out', screenshot the ten-question list and glance at the FAQ.

journey.quote: Greece wedding packages usually bundle the ceremony, its set-up, a coordinator and some help with the paperwork.
journey.reaction: There it is. Second sentence, uses my exact search words, gives me the answer. Good.

journey.quote: Exclusive use, guest rooms, transfers and outside suppliers are where packages differ most, so ask about each in writing.
journey.reaction: Useful. I didn't know rooms and transfers were the tricky bits. This is the bullet I'd remember.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: AUD again? I'm in Singapore. Is this only for Australians?

journey.section: What a Greek venue package usually includes
journey.quote: Read enough Greek package documents and a shape appears.
journey.reaction: Nice line, but then it's paragraph after paragraph of one hotel at a time. On my phone I wanted a quick bullet list of the usual inclusions first, then the venue detail if I care.

journey.quote: Pathos and Eros add your own event coordinator.
journey.reaction: Concrete. Named packages, guest counts up to 10, 20 or 30, and what the bigger ones add. That's the kind of detail I came for.

journey.quote: Its weddings page still links the 2025-2026 brochure, so ask for the terms that apply to a 2027 date.
journey.reaction: Dated and honest about it. Answers my 'is this still true?' question before I ask.

journey.quote: [Mystique](https://mystique.gr/weddings/), also in Oia, offers wedding specialists and getting ready in a suite, without a published package.
journey.reaction: Santorini is the island I'd actually look at, and it's mostly 'no published package', 'proposal on request', 'no tiers published'. Fair, but I end the section knowing what they don't publish more than what I'd get.

journey.quote: Its document is direct: "Symbolic weddings /renewal of vows are not legally recognized from the Greek constitution."
journey.reaction: Oh, that's important. I'd assumed a beach ceremony in Greece just counts. Glad it says so plainly.

journey.quote: DFAT can issue a CNI in Australia, but some local authorities accept only one issued in their own country.
journey.reaction: This whole legal bit is written for Australians. Not my country, so I skip it.

journey.quote: In peak season, traffic congestion is severe in the main cities and on the islands, and only licensed taxis with the meter running should be used.
journey.reaction: Heading is about what the package covers, then suddenly taxi meter advice. Not wrong, just a bit off-topic for a packages page.

journey.quote: Euphoria's packages "are complete packages, and their items are not interchangeable", with no refund or alternative for a service you skip.
journey.reaction: Good to know before I fall for a 'package'. This section is the most useful part for me.

journey.section: How to compare two quotes like for like
journey.quote: If one quote answers a point and the other is silent, the silent one is not cheaper. It is unfinished.
journey.reaction: Love this line, and the ten-point list above it is the thing I'd screenshot and bookmark.

journey.quote: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.reaction: Heading tells me it's not for me, so I skip straight past. At least it's labelled honestly.

journey.quote: Rarely in the sense most couples mean.
journey.reaction: Straight answer in the first words, then examples. That's how I want an FAQ.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a Greek wedding package cost? Even a ballpark. There isn't a single price on the page.
Is this service for people outside Australia, or only Australians?
Which island has the most packages for a small wedding of around 30 to 50 guests?

turn_offs_found.quote: Read enough Greek package documents and a shape appears.
turn_offs_found.why: The section that matches my search heading opens with scene-setting and then runs as long venue-by-venue paragraphs. Skimming on a phone, I want the usual inclusions as a short list up top; as it is, I have to read five hotels to rebuild the list myself.

turn_offs_found.quote: [Mystique](https://mystique.gr/weddings/), also in Oia, offers wedding specialists and getting ready in a suite, without a published package.
turn_offs_found.why: Island by island, most entries end on 'without a published package' or 'proposal on request'. Skimming, I keep landing on the gaps rather than what each island does offer, so the section feels thinner than it is.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
turn_offs_found.why: It's the first thing after the takeaways, and with the Australian legal and insurance sections later it makes me think the site isn't for me. I'd be less likely to bookmark if I'm not sure they work with non-Australians.

would_share_with: My friend who just got engaged and is collecting quotes; I'd send her the ten-question comparison list and the 'What packages often leave out' section

cta_reaction.quote: compare your quotes with a Wedded Advisor
cta_reaction.why: I don't have quotes yet, I'm just looking. No pop-ups and the links didn't get in my way, so no complaints. I'd bookmark before I'd enquire, and the AUD line makes me unsure they'd work with me.

top_3_changes: Open 'What a Greek venue package usually includes' with a short bullet list of the common inclusions (ceremony set-up, coordinator, flowers, sparkling wine and cake, paperwork help, a couple's gesture), then give the venue detail below it.
In 'Island by island', lead each island with what its venues do offer (ceremony spaces, guest sizes, specialists) and fold the 'no published package' notes into one short line per island.
Phrase the early AUD line so it doesn't read as Australians-only, for example by noting AUD quoting as a benefit for Australian couples rather than the only thing said about the service.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on a phone
No invented brand facts; missing info went to unanswered_questions
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Person-set title, deferred business details and deliberately unprinted prices not treated as must-fix; no request for sourcing lines

assumptions: Persona is provisional (weight 0.10); reactions reflect generic informational search intent.

Arrived from a Google search for 'greece wedding packages' on a phone; read the intro and takeaways, skimmed the inclusions and island sections, read 'What packages often leave out' and the comparison list, skipped the Australian section, then the FAQ.
Prices are deliberately not printed; the missing ballpark is logged as an unanswered question only.
Fees, Wedded Privileges and company specifics are deferred, so the Wedded Concierge 'fourth route' paragraph was not judged.
Read with images not yet loaded; image slots and HTML comments judged as invisible.
Quotes with inline HTML fact comments, link markup or bold markers are given as a reader sees them, except where link markup is kept so the quote matches the draft text.
